title: Pedunculoside ameliorates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease by targeting HNRNPA1 and modulating PPARalpha signaling pathway to enhance Mitochondrial Fatty Acid beta-Oxidation.
authors: Zhou, Yang; Chi, Jingyun; Xu, Xining; Zhu, Rongrong; Wang, Tianhao; Zhang, Tao; Hong, Dandan; Fu, Huazhou; Zhou, Xizhen; Zhao, Kun
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然产物Pedunculoside通过结合HNRNPA1调控PPARalpha信号通路改善代谢相关脂肪肝病，虽涉及分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as a significant global health challenge, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic agents that offer enhanced efficacy and improved safety. Pedunculoside (PE), a naturally occurring triterpenoid saponin, has demonstrated promising lipid-modulating properties. Nevertheless, its precise mechanisms of action in the context of MASLD remain unclear. PURPOSE: To investigate the anti-MASLD effect of PE and uncover its novel mechanism via targeting heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A1 (HNRNPA1) and regulating downstream PPARalpha pathway. METHOD: The therapeutic potential of PE was evaluated both in primary mouse hepatocytes and in vivo using high-fat, high-cholesterol (HFHC) and high-fat diet (HFD) induced MASLD mouse models. A multi-omics and multi-technique approach was applied, including biochemical assays, histopathology, transcriptomic and lipidomic profiling, alongside target-engagement validation via drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), surface plasmon resonance (SPR), molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and HNRNPA1 knockout models. RESULTS: PE significantly improved key metabolic and histological features in MASLD models. Mechanistically, PE was found to directly bind HNRNPA1 (a previously unreported target in MASLD therapeutics). This interaction enhanced the mRNA stability of PPARalpha, leading to activation of fatty acid beta-oxidation. Crucially, HNRNPA1 knockout abolished the beneficial effects of PE, confirming the functional necessity of the PE-HNRNPA1-PPARalpha axis in vivo. CONCLUSION: Our study uncovers a novel therapeutic axis in MASLD, in which PE enhances the stability of PPARalpha mRNA by directly binding to HNRNPA1, and consequently upregulates fatty acid beta-oxidation. These findings not only position PE as a promising therapeutic candidate for MASLD but also identify the HNRNPA1-PPARalpha regulatory pathway as a potential mechanistic target for treating metabolic liver diseases.
abstract_zh: 背景：代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝病（MASLD）已成为全球重大健康挑战，凸显了对具有更强疗效和更佳安全性的新型治疗药物的迫切需求。齿孔酸（Pedunculoside, PE）作为一种天然三萜皂苷，已显示出有前景的脂质调节特性。然而，其在MASLD中的确切作用机制仍不清楚。目的：探讨PE的抗MASLD效应，并揭示其通过靶向异质核核糖核蛋白A1（HNRNPA1）及调控下游PPARalpha通路的新机制。方法：在原代小鼠肝细胞及体内实验中，利用高脂高胆固醇（HFHC）和高脂饮食（HFD）诱导的MASLD小鼠模型评估PE的治疗潜力。采用多组学和多技术方法，包括生化检测、组织病理学、转录组学和脂质组学分析，以及通过药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）、表面等离子体共振（SPR）、分子对接、分子动力学模拟和HNRNPA1敲除模型进行靶点结合验证。结果：PE显著改善了MASLD模型中的关键代谢和组织学特征。机制上，发现PE直接结合HNRNPA1（这是MASLD治疗中此前未报道的靶点）。这种相互作用增强了PPARalpha的mRNA稳定性，从而激活脂肪酸β-氧化。关键的是，HNRNPA1敲除消除了PE的有益效应，证实了PE-HNRNPA1-PPARalpha轴在体内的功能必要性。结论：我们的研究揭示了MASLD中的一个新型治疗轴，其中PE通过直接结合HNRNPA1增强PPARalpha mRNA的稳定性，进而上调脂肪酸β-氧化。这些发现不仅将PE定位为MASLD的有前景治疗候选药物，还将HNRNPA1-PPARalpha调控通路确定为治疗代谢性肝病的潜在机制靶点。
